SQL.overview: Standard query language text typically transmitted over proprietary database wire protocols like TDS or PostgreSQL Wire Protocol.
disadvantages: Transport protocol varies by vendor
Vulnerable to injection if not parameterized
SQL.security: Relies on underlying wire protocol encryption (e.g., TLS)

Redis (RESP).overview: REdis Serialization Protocol, a simple, human-readable text-based protocol used for communication between Redis clients and the Redis server.
disadvantages: Text-based nature adds slight overhead compared to pure binary
Lacks native advanced streaming semantics without RESP3
Redis (RESP).security: Supports TLS (since Redis 6) and simple password authentication (AUTH)

MongoDB Wire.overview: A socket-based, request-response binary protocol used for communication with MongoDB databases.
advantages: Binary format is efficient for BSON data
disadvantages: Specific to MongoDB ecosystem
Complex driver implementation required
MongoDB Wire.security: Supports TLS/SSL and SASL authentication mechanisms (SCRAM)

S3.overview: Amazon Simple Storage Service REST API, utilizing HTTP/HTTPS for object storage operations like PUT, GET, and DELETE.
advantages: Ubiquitous industry standard for object storage
disadvantages: HTTP overhead per request
Eventual consistency on some operations historically
S3.security: IAM policies, SigV4 request signing, TLS, Server-Side Encryption (SSE)

JDBC.overview: Java Database Connectivity API and associated driver protocols for connecting Java applications to various relational databases.
disadvantages: Heavyweight driver dependencies
Synchronous blocking API historically
JDBC.security: Relies on underlying driver and database security configurations

ODBC.overview: Open Database Connectivity, a standard C programming interface for accessing database management systems.
advantages: Supported by almost all BI and analytical tools
disadvantages: Complex driver configuration (DSN)
Can add latency due to abstraction layer
ODBC.security: Relies on database-specific driver security (e.g., encrypted connections)

CQL.overview: Cassandra Query Language native binary protocol, used for asynchronous communication with Apache Cassandra clusters.
advantages: Native asynchronous support (multiplexing on single connection)
disadvantages: Not a full relational SQL language
Driver complexity for token-aware routing
CQL.security: Client-to-node TLS encryption and internal SASL authentication

Memcached.overview: A simple, text or binary based protocol for setting, getting, and managing key-value pairs in a distributed memory caching system.
disadvantages: Lacks persistence mechanisms
Very limited data types (strings/bytes only)
Memcached.security: SASL authentication, typically deployed in isolated private networks

Firebase.overview: Realtime database synchronization protocol utilizing WebSockets for long-lived bidirectional state syncing.
advantages: Automatic state resolution and offline support
disadvantages: Vendor lock-in to Google Cloud
Complex pricing model based on connections/reads
Firebase.security: Firebase Security Rules, Google IAM, TLS for transport

Elasticsearch (HTTP).overview: RESTful API over HTTP using JSON payloads for indexing, searching, and managing distributed Lucene-based search clusters.
advantages: Easy to interact with via standard HTTP clients
disadvantages: JSON parsing overhead for massive datasets
Verbose query syntax
Elasticsearch (HTTP).security: Role-based access control, TLS, API keys

Cassandra CQL.overview: The native binary transport protocol for Apache Cassandra, optimized for asynchronous, pipelined queries across a distributed ring.
advantages: Allows multiple concurrent requests on one connection
disadvantages: Custom serialization required
Tightly coupled to Cassandra architecture
Cassandra CQL.security: Client-to-node encryption, node-to-node TLS, role-based access control

Neo4j Bolt.overview: A connection-oriented protocol over TCP designed for efficient communication with graph databases, using the PackStream serialization format.
disadvantages: Specific to Neo4j graph databases
More complex to implement than HTTP REST
Neo4j Bolt.security: TLS encryption, basic auth, Kerberos integration

Gremlin.overview: A graph traversal language and associated protocol (typically over WebSockets) for Apache TinkerPop-enabled graph databases.
disadvantages: Steep learning curve
Performance varies heavily by backend implementation

DynamoDB API.overview: AWS proprietary REST-like API over HTTP/HTTPS using JSON payloads for accessing the DynamoDB NoSQL database service.
disadvantages: AWS vendor lock-in
1MB limit per query/scan page
DynamoDB API.security: AWS IAM for fine-grained access control, TLS, KMS for encryption at rest

CosmosDB API.overview: Multi-model database API over HTTP/HTTPS (supporting SQL, MongoDB, Gremlin, etc.) natively utilizing a custom binary protocol or REST for Azure Cosmos DB.
advantages: Supports multiple wire protocols for compatibility
Direct TCP mode reduces latency significantly
disadvantages: Azure vendor lock-in
Direct mode requires specific network configuration

HDFS.overview: Hadoop Distributed File System protocol, typically involving an RPC mechanism over TCP to coordinate NameNodes and DataNodes.
disadvantages: High latency for small file operations
Single point of failure (historically) at the NameNode

NFS.overview: Network File System, a distributed file system protocol allowing a user on a client computer to access files over a computer network much like local storage.
disadvantages: Performance degradation over high-latency WANs
Stateful nature can complicate failover (NFSv4)

SMB/CIFS.overview: Server Message Block / Common Internet File System, a network file sharing protocol primarily used in Windows environments for shared access to files, printers, and serial ports.
advantages: Supports advanced features like oplocks and transparent failover
disadvantages: Chatty protocol, poor performance on high-latency links
Historically vulnerable to exploits (e.g., EternalBlue)

iSCSI.overview: Internet Small Computer Systems Interface, an IP-based storage networking standard for linking data storage facilities by carrying SCSI commands over IP networks.
advantages: Presents as local block storage to the OS
disadvantages: High overhead compared to local NVMe
Requires network optimization (Jumbo frames) for best performance
iSCSI.security: CHAP authentication, IPsec for transport encryption

IP.overview: Internet Protocol, the principal communications protocol in the Internet protocol suite for relaying datagrams across network boundaries (routing).
disadvantages: Best-effort delivery (no inherent reliability guarantee)
Vulnerable to spoofing if routers do not implement BCP38
IP.security: IPsec can be applied, otherwise relies on upper layers (TLS)

IPv4.overview: Internet Protocol version 4, the fourth version of IP and the most widely deployed, utilizing 32-bit addresses.
advantages: Universally supported by all networked hardware
disadvantages: Address exhaustion (only ~4.3 billion addresses)
Requires NAT, which breaks end-to-end connectivity principle
IPv4.security: IPsec supported but rarely native, easily spoofed without network protections

IPv6.overview: Internet Protocol version 6, designed to replace IPv4, utilizing 128-bit addresses to solve the address exhaustion problem.
disadvantages: Complex coexistence with IPv4
Human-unreadable addresses
IPv6.security: IPsec support is mandated by specification

ICMP.overview: Internet Control Message Protocol, used by network devices to send error messages and operational information indicating success or failure of communication.
disadvantages: Can be weaponized for DDoS (Smurf attacks, Ping floods)
Often blocked by overly aggressive firewalls, breaking PMTUD
ICMP.security: No inherent encryption, prone to spoofing

DNS.overview: Domain Name System, a hierarchical and decentralized naming system used to resolve human-readable domain names to IP addresses.
advantages: Highly distributed and resilient caching architecture
Essential for human interaction with the internet
disadvantages: Historically unencrypted (vulnerable to eavesdropping/hijacking)
UDP transport makes it susceptible to amplification attacks
DNS.security: DNSSEC for integrity, DNS over HTTPS (DoH) / DNS over TLS (DoT) for privacy

BGP.overview: Border Gateway Protocol, the exterior gateway protocol designed to exchange routing and reachability information among autonomous systems (AS) on the Internet.
advantages: Highly scalable to the entire internet routing table
Extensive policy control via route attributes
disadvantages: Slow convergence time during topology changes
Based on implicit trust (vulnerable to route leaks/hijacks)
BGP.security: RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) for route validation, TCP MD5/AO for peer authentication

TLS.overview: Transport Layer Security, a cryptographic protocol designed to provide communications security over a computer network.
advantages: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) in modern versions (TLS 1.3)
disadvantages: Handshake adds latency (mitigated in TLS 1.3)
Certificate management complexity
TLS.security: Uses asymmetric cryptography for key exchange and symmetric for payload

SSL.overview: Secure Sockets Layer, the deprecated predecessor to TLS, designed to secure transport layer connections.
advantages: Supported by very old legacy hardware
disadvantages: Cryptographically broken (POODLE, DROWN attacks)
Completely deprecated by IETF
SSL.security: Considered insecure; disabled in modern browsers and OSs

IPsec.overview: Internet Protocol Security, a secure network protocol suite that authenticates and encrypts the packets of data to provide secure encrypted communication between two computers over an IP network.
advantages: Operates transparently at the network layer
Highly robust standard supported by most enterprise firewalls
disadvantages: Notoriously complex to configure
Can be blocked by NAT/Firewalls if ESP is dropped
IPsec.security: Provides AH (Authentication Header) and ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)

MAC.overview: Media Access Control, the lower sublayer of the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) responsible for hardware addressing and access control mechanisms on physical network media.
advantages: Enables local network communication without routing
disadvantages: Not routable across different networks
Easily spoofed in software
MAC.security: Vulnerable to MAC flooding and spoofing; mitigated by switch port security (802.1X)

ARP.overview: Address Resolution Protocol, used for discovering the link layer address (MAC) associated with a given internet layer address (IPv4).
advantages: Essential mechanism for IPv4 local delivery
disadvantages: Stateless and unauthenticated
Relies entirely on broadcast domains
ARP.security: Highly vulnerable to ARP spoofing/poisoning and Man-in-the-Middle attacks

DHCP.overview: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol, a network management protocol used to dynamically assign an IP address and other network configuration parameters to devices.
advantages: Efficient recycling of IP addresses via leases
disadvantages: Relies on broadcasts, requiring relay agents across subnets
Unauthenticated by default
DHCP.security: Vulnerable to Rogue DHCP servers and DHCP starvation

SNMP.overview: Simple Network Management Protocol, an Internet Standard protocol for collecting, organizing, and modifying information about managed devices on IP networks.
disadvantages: SNMPv1/v2c send community strings in plaintext
Complex ASN.1/BER encoding scheme
SNMP.security: SNMPv3 provides strong authentication and encryption (USM/VACM)

VLAN.overview: Virtual Local Area Network (IEEE 802.1Q), a layer 2 protocol used to partition and isolate broadcast domains on a computer network at the data link layer.
advantages: Simplifies network design and security policy enforcement
disadvantages: Limited to 4094 VLANs per domain
Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) complexities
VLAN.security: Vulnerable to VLAN hopping if native VLANs are misconfigured

VXLAN.overview: Virtual Extensible LAN, a network virtualization technology that attempts to address scalability problems associated with large cloud computing deployments by encapsulating MAC-based L2 frames within L3 UDP packets.
useCases: Stretching L2 domains across L3 boundaries
advantages: Leverages ECMP in L3 networks for better bandwidth utilization
disadvantages: Encapsulation overhead adds to MTU requirements
Requires complex control planes (like BGP EVPN)
VXLAN.security: No inherent encryption; relies on underlying transport security like IPsec

WireGuard.overview: A modern, high-performance VPN protocol utilizing state-of-the-art cryptography, designed to be simpler and faster than IPsec and OpenVPN.
advantages: Extremely small codebase (~4000 lines) for easy auditing
In-kernel implementation provides exceptional throughput and low latency
disadvantages: Uses UDP only, which can be blocked by restrictive firewalls
Lacks native dynamic IP assignment mechanisms natively

OpenVPN.overview: A widely used, open-source virtual private network protocol and software that uses custom security protocols utilizing SSL/TLS for key exchange.
advantages: Can operate over TCP 443 to bypass strict firewalls
disadvantages: Heavyweight userspace implementation impacts performance
Complex configuration and certificate management
OpenVPN.security: Robust security utilizing OpenSSL libraries; supports custom cipher suites

IKEv2.overview: Internet Key Exchange version 2, the protocol used to set up a security association (SA) in the IPsec protocol suite.
advantages: Native support in iOS, Android, macOS, Windows
MOBIKE extension allows seamless network transitions
disadvantages: Can be difficult to troubleshoot SA mismatches
Often blocked by restrictive NATs/Firewalls
IKEv2.security: Strong asymmetric authentication (RSA/ECDSA or EAP) to bootstrap IPsec

L2TP.overview: Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol, used to support virtual private networks or as part of the delivery of services by ISPs; it does not provide encryption by itself.
advantages: Native support in many legacy systems
Can transport non-IP protocols by tunneling PPP
disadvantages: No native confidentiality; requires IPsec for security
Performance overhead due to double encapsulation
L2TP.security: Insecure on its own; always paired with IPsec in enterprise environments

PPTP.overview: Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol, an obsolete method for implementing virtual private networks natively supported by older Windows versions.
advantages: Built into almost every OS natively
Low CPU overhead due to weak encryption
disadvantages: Fundamentally compromised security
GRE protocol 47 is often blocked by NAT routers
PPTP.security: Considered completely insecure; vulnerable to offline dictionary attacks

FTP.overview: File Transfer Protocol, a standard network protocol used for the transfer of computer files between a client and server on a computer network.
advantages: Optimized strictly for bulk file transfer
disadvantages: Transmits credentials and data in cleartext
Active/Passive modes cause NAT and firewall traversal issues
FTP.security: No inherent security; replaced by SFTP and FTPS

SFTP.overview: SSH File Transfer Protocol, a network protocol that provides file access, file transfer, and file management over any reliable data stream (typically SSH).
advantages: Uses a single port (22), making firewall configuration trivial
Inherits robust SSH security and authentication
disadvantages: Can be slower than pure FTP due to SSH encryption overhead
Less native support in older Windows environments
SFTP.security: Highly secure, utilizing SSH cryptographic primitives

FTPS.overview: FTP over SSL/TLS, an extension to the commonly used File Transfer Protocol that adds support for the Transport Layer Security (TLS) and the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) cryptographic protocols.
advantages: Maintains FTP command structure while securing transit
disadvantages: Inherits FTP's firewall and NAT issues
More complex to setup than SFTP

SMTP.overview: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, the internet standard communication protocol for electronic mail transmission.
advantages: Universal standard for global email interoperability
disadvantages: Lacks native sender authentication
Chatty, text-based protocol
SMTP.security: Secured via STARTTLS; spoofing mitigated via SPF, DKIM, and DMARC

POP3.overview: Post Office Protocol version 3, an application-layer internet standard protocol used by e-mail clients to retrieve e-mail from a mail server.
disadvantages: Poor experience across multiple devices
Lacks server-side folder synchronization

IMAP.overview: Internet Message Access Protocol, an Internet standard protocol used by email clients to retrieve and manage email messages from a mail server over a TCP/IP connection.
advantages: Allows partial downloads (headers only) for fast UI loading
disadvantages: Requires significantly more server storage than POP3
Complex protocol synchronization states

SSH.overview: Secure Shell, a cryptographic network protocol for operating network services securely over an unsecured network, most notably remote command-line login.
advantages: Supports strong public-key authentication and local/remote port forwarding
disadvantages: Key management at scale requires infrastructure
Vulnerable to brute-force if password auth is left enabled
SSH.security: Highly secure, utilizing asymmetric keys for auth and symmetric ciphers for transport

Telnet.overview: Teletype Network, an application protocol used on the Internet or local area network to provide a bidirectional interactive text-oriented communication facility using a virtual terminal connection.
advantages: Extremely simple and universally available client
disadvantages: Transmits everything, including passwords, in absolute cleartext
Completely lacks server authentication
Telnet.security: Zero inherent security; wholly deprecated in favor of SSH

LDAP.overview: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol, an open, vendor-neutral, industry standard application protocol for accessing and maintaining distributed directory information services.
advantages: Industry standard for enterprise authentication integration
disadvantages: Complex query syntax and schema management
Historically unencrypted by default
LDAP.security: Secured via LDAPS (Port 636) or STARTTLS; supports SASL authentication

Internal.overview: A generic classification for proprietary or unexposed intra-system communication protocols used exclusively within a secure backend boundary.
advantages: Can bypass standard authentication layers for performance
Tailored exactly to system needs without standard compliance overhead
disadvantages: Lacks interoperability with third-party tools
Security often relies solely on network perimeter (Zero Trust violation)
Internal.security: Often unencrypted (assuming network safety) or secured via mutual TLS (mTLS)

IPC.overview: Inter-Process Communication, mechanisms provided by an operating system for processes to manage shared data and communicate with each other.
IPC.transport: OS Kernels, Shared Memory, Unix Domain Sockets
useCases: Communication between a web server and application server on the same host
advantages: Bypasses the network stack entirely, offering microsecond latency
disadvantages: Strictly limited to a single physical or virtual machine
Implementation varies wildly between operating systems
IPC.security: Secured by OS-level file permissions and process isolation boundaries

gopher.overview: An early Internet distributed document search and retrieval protocol, designed to distribute, search, and retrieve documents in a highly structured, menu-driven manner.
advantages: Extremely lightweight and simple text parsing
Strict hierarchical structure organizes data cleanly
disadvantages: Lacked rich media and hyperlinking flexibility of HTML/HTTP
Completely superseded by the World Wide Web
gopher.security: No native encryption or authentication mechanisms

BitTorrent.overview: A decentralized, peer-to-peer communication protocol for distributing data and electronic files over the Internet in a highly efficient manner.
advantages: Downloads get faster as more peers join (scalable)
Highly resilient to single server failures
disadvantages: Suffers from the free-rider problem without private trackers
Often blocked by ISPs due to association with piracy
BitTorrent.security: Protocol Encryption (PE/MSE) obfuscates traffic, but IP addresses are public in the swarm

IPFS.overview: InterPlanetary File System, a peer-to-peer hypermedia protocol designed to preserve and grow humanity's knowledge by making the web upgradeable, resilient, and more open via content addressing.
advantages: Files are addressed by cryptographic hash, ensuring immutability
disadvantages: Files can disappear if no node pins (hosts) them
High resource usage for running a full node compared to HTTP clients
IPFS.security: Inherent data integrity via hashing; transport secured via libp2p secure channels

ActivityPub.overview: A decentralized social networking protocol based on the ActivityStreams 2.0 data format, providing a federated server-to-server API for delivering notifications and content.
advantages: Enables interoperability between completely different social platforms
Prevents single-entity control over social graphs
disadvantages: Complex moderation and anti-abuse across instances
High server costs for federating massive instances
ActivityPub.security: Relies on HTTPS, HTTP Signatures, and JSON-LD for request authentication between instances

Matrix.overview: An open standard for interoperable, decentralized, real-time communication over IP, utilizing JSON over REST to synchronize state across a federation of servers.
advantages: Bridges allow connection to legacy networks (Slack, Discord, IRC)
disadvantages: Heavy server resource consumption (Synapse) for large rooms
Complex cryptographic key management for end users
Matrix.security: End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) built-in using the Olm/Megolm cryptographic ratchets

SIP.overview: Session Initiation Protocol, a signaling protocol used for initiating, maintaining, and terminating real-time sessions that include voice, video and messaging applications.
advantages: Industry standard for telecommunications over IP
disadvantages: Notoriously difficult to traverse NATs without STUN/TURN/ICE
Only handles signaling, requires RTP for actual media transport
SIP.security: SIPS (SIP over TLS) for signaling encryption; vulnerable to toll fraud if improperly configured

VoIP.overview: Voice over Internet Protocol, a broader methodology and group of technologies for the delivery of voice communications and multimedia sessions over Internet Protocol networks.
advantages: Drastically reduces telecommunication costs compared to PSTN
Integrates voice directly into digital workflows
disadvantages: Highly sensitive to network jitter, latency, and packet loss
Requires QoS (Quality of Service) configurations on enterprise networks
VoIP.security: SRTP (Secure Real-time Transport Protocol) for encrypting media streams
